markdown_report:
SASRec supplies a feasible starting point, but the diagnoses favor testing recent intent and ranking discrimination before adding complex latent-interest machinery. No improvement is established yet.

**Insights.** From the starting point: (1) causal attention can combine recent and older interactions, but does not explicitly control stale-interest influence; this matches the reported current-purpose failures. (2) shared item embeddings provide efficient scoring, but broad associations need not imply immediate usefulness. (3) strong average training margins can conceal difficult cases: Electronics has 14.95% sampled wrong ranks, versus 3.03% for Movies_and_TV; neither establishes validation HR@10.

From related work: (1) LSIDN and IDCLRec motivate separating persistent interests from dynamic intent, without claiming to observe motivations. (2) TLSTSRec motivates adaptive recent/history fusion; an interaction-only gate avoids unavailable demographic inputs. (3) gSASRec motivates multiple-negative training, while R²NS warns that premature hard mining can hurt. The embedding alignment scores near 0.54 do not justify prioritizing collapse regularization.

**Framework.** Three complementary directions organize the search:

| Direction | Existing mechanism | Proposed minimal experiment |
|---|---|---|
| Temporal representation | SASRec; LSIDN; TLSTSRec | Gated recent-window residual |
| Ranking discrimination | gSASRec; R²NS | Uniform multiple-negative objective |
| Directed association | Transition graphs; PCTM | Training-only transition-score blend |

**Candidate assessments.** Scores are originality/potential/user alignment/model alignment/difficulty; higher difficulty means harder implementation. Each assessment gives a benefit and limitation, respectively.

- **Gated recent residual: 4/7/8/6/3.** Originality: interaction-only adaptation / familiar fusion; potential: cheap extension / limited novelty; user alignment: targets stale interests and diluted specific preferences / cannot establish compatibility; model alignment: may improve difficult distinctions / weak margins may originate elsewhere; difficulty: shared embeddings / predictor and causal pooling require updates.
- **Multiple-negative gBCE: 2/7/5/9/3.** Originality: established method / little novelty; potential: reusable objective / sampling sensitivity; user alignment: stronger discrimination / no explicit temporal mechanism; model alignment: directly targets sampled separation / training margins may not generalize; difficulty: vectorized / memory cost.
- **Directed transition blend: 4/7/7/6/4.** Originality: useful adaptation / established counts; potential: complementary signal / sparse edges; user alignment: ordered associations / no verified complement labels; model alignment: alternative ranking evidence / may amplify popularity; difficulty: sparse implementation / inference integration.

**Selected idea: gated recent-window residual.** At 0% progress, prioritize a small architectural change. It explicitly targets stale historical influence and broadly plausible recommendations diluting repeated recent interests. Its model-facing hypothesis is improved lower-tail separation, particularly in Electronics.

At every valid position, pool the latest five causal item embeddings, project them, and learn a residual gate from historical features, recent features, their agreement, and observed prefix length. Initialize the residual near zero. Retain baseline training loss to isolate this intervention; compare with fixed fusion and baseline under the same seeds and budget. Select exclusively by pinned four-category macro validation HR@10. Compatibility, redundancy, and actual current intent remain unobserved.

idea.description: Add a gated recent-window residual to each per-dataset SASRec model. A causal recent-interest representation supplements the historical representation used for next-item scoring.
idea.motivation: The user diagnosis identifies stale historical influence and dilution of specific recent preferences by broad associations. Electronics also exhibits the weakest sampled ranking separation. Recent fusion addresses the first two failures directly as a hypothesis and may improve the measured separation failure; validation must establish usefulness.
idea.implementation_notes: Preserve DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], all four dataset routes, original splits, preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, and the effective SASREC_EPOCHS default of 200. Use shared item embeddings and causal, padding-masked pooling over at most five items. Set r_t = W(pool_t), g_t = sigmoid(MLP([h_t, r_t, cosine(h_t,r_t), log1p(prefix_length)])), and z_t = h_t + g_t*r_t. Initialize the final gate bias to -3. Retain the baseline objective and optimizer for the initial comparison. Save architecture settings and weights beneath the trial directory; update the predictor writer so working/predict.py reconstructs this architecture. Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis). view.model must reference the trained module; log2feats must return fused features and predict_score must use the identical inference scoring rule. Report measured margins and their definitions; omit unavailable category attribution, review signals, and simulator traits. Keep single-GPU execution and account for all training and diagnostics within the shared budget. No experiment has been executed.
idea.pseudocode:
for dataset in FOUR_DATASETS:
    initialize baseline SASRec and recent residual with seed=42
    for batch in unchanged_training_loader:
        h = sasrec.causal_features(sequence)
        recent = masked_causal_mean(item_emb(sequence), window=5)
        r = recent_projection(recent)
        length = cumulative_nonpadding_count(sequence)
        gate = sigmoid(gate_mlp(concat(h, r, cosine(h, r), log1p(length))))
        z = h + gate * r
        loss = baseline_loss(z, positive, negative)
        update_parameters(loss)
    save_model_and_architecture_under_trial_directory()
write_predictor_using_identical_fused_features_and_dataset_routing()
# Host independently evaluates the pinned validation benchmark.
# Compare baseline, fixed fusion, and learned fusion by macro validation HR@10.

originality.positive: A small interaction-only adaptation connects recent-preference failures to an explicit causal residual.
originality.negative: Long/short interest fusion and learned gates are established techniques.

future_potential.positive: Provides a low-cost foundation for later timestamp-aware fusion and ranking-objective experiments.
future_potential.negative: Recent interactions do not establish intent, product compatibility, or unsatisfied demand.

code_difficulty.positive: Requires only masked pooling, a projection, and a small gate while sharing item embeddings.
code_difficulty.negative: Training, generated inference, and diagnostic feature paths must agree exactly.

related_work.title: Self-Attentive Sequential Recommendation
contributions: Provides the causal attention baseline and shared item scoring architecture.
limitations: Does not explicitly separate persistent preference from immediate intent.

related_work.title: LSIDN
contributions: Separates long-term preferences and short-term behavior through dedicated modeling and denoising.
limitations: Inferred interests do not establish actual user motivations.

related_work.title: IDCLRec
contributions: Models consistent interests and residual dynamic intent.
limitations: Its intent machinery is more complex than the proposed initial experiment.

related_work.title: TLSTSRec
contributions: Motivates adaptive fusion of temporal, long-term, and short-term information.
limitations: Does not establish gains for this four-category benchmark or the proposed residual.

related_work.title: gSASRec
contributions: Motivates generalized BCE with multiple negatives to address sampled-BCE overconfidence.
limitations: Additional negatives increase computation and do not explicitly address stale preferences.

related_work.title: R²NS
contributions: Motivates uniform warm-up and gradual stochastic hard-negative selection.
limitations: Hard negatives can include unobserved positives.

related_work.title: Do Sequential Recommendation Benchmarks Require Higher-Order Sequence Modelling?
contributions: Motivates a lightweight transition-count alternative using recency, smoothing, and popularity adjustment.
limitations: Observed transitions do not establish complementary function or compatibility.
